context.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud, providing sub-50ms decisions and case management for human analysts. It operates under strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and budget constraints in AWS eu-west-1.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer
- Fraud Screening Engine (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management UI
- AWS RDS PostgreSQL
- AWS S3
- AWS SNS / SQS

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway sends synchronous authorization requests via HTTPS/JSON to Fraud Screening Engine (3,000 TPS, 30ms timeout).
- Fraud Screening Engine fetches model rules from S3 and publishes audit logs to RDS PostgreSQL and S3.
- Fraud Analyst Workstation accesses Case Management UI asynchronously over TLS.
- AWS SNS/SQS pushes model updates to the Fraud Screening Engine.

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration chosen for operational simplicity within the 3-engineer team constraint.
- AWS S3: Versioned model storage and tamper-evident object lock audit logs.
- AWS RDS PostgreSQL: Structured storage for HMAC-chained audit logs and case management.
- AWS SNS/SQS: Asynchronous pub/sub pattern for zero-downtime model hot-swaps.
- AWS CloudWatch: Centralized metrics and structured JSON logging for observability.

## Rationale
This architecture uses proven, managed AWS primitives to maintain low operational overhead for a three-engineer team within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. It decouples high-throughput synchronous scoring from asynchronous tasks to guarantee strict P99 latency and high availability.

## Overview
A real-time payment fraud screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations within 50 ms at P99 while enabling fraud analysts to review suspicious transactions. It maintains PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability within a €25k monthly AWS budget.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst (Person)
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer (External System)
- API Gateway / Ingestion Container (AWS API Gateway / Envoy proxy)
- High-Performance Scoring Engine (AWS ECS on Fargate)
- Feature Store (Redis)
- Async Event Bus (AWS EventBridge / SQS)
- Case Management Web Application (AWS ECS on Fargate)
- Model & Rule Registry Container
- Audit & Compliance Storage (AWS S3 with Object Lock and Parquet format)
- Configuration & Secrets Management (AWS Secrets Manager / Parameter Store)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway to API Gateway / Ingestion Container via HTTPS/TLS
- API Gateway to High-Performance Scoring Engine via internal VPC gRPC/REST
- Scoring Engine to Feature Store via Redis Protocol
- Scoring Engine to Async Event Bus via AWS SDK (JSON/Protobuf over SQS/EventBridge)
- Async Event Bus to Case Management and Audit Storage via AWS SQS/SNS
- Fraud Analyst to Case Management Web Application via HTTPS/TLS

## Technology Stack
- AWS (eu-west-1): Cloud provider and regional infrastructure
- AWS ECS on Fargate: Stateless container hosting for predictable scaling within budget
- Redis: In-memory feature store for ultra-low latency lookups (R-04)
- AWS S3 Object Lock: Tamper-evident, cost-effective 7-year audit storage (R-06)
- AWS API Gateway / Envoy: Ingress security, rate limiting, and tokenization stripping (R-05)
- JSON Schema / Protobuf: Strongly typed, backward-compatible event contracts

## Rationale
Stateless Fargate containers combined with an in-memory Redis feature store achieve the sub-50ms latency requirement (R-04) within the €25k budget. AWS S3 Object Lock and decoupled asynchronous event processing ensure PCI-DSS compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability (R-06) without impacting real-time transaction performance.

API Gateway / Ingestion Container.analysis:
## Overview
The API Gateway / Ingestion Container serves as the secure edge proxy for the Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system, handling external ingress, request validation, and routing. It screens payment authorizations in real time while enforcing strict PCI-DSS compliance and latency constraints.

## Key Elements
- API Gateway / Ingestion Container: AWS API Gateway and Envoy proxy
- High-Performance Scoring Engine: Internal downstream service
- Feature Store / Cache: Redis for idempotency and token caching
- External Systems: Payment Gateway / Acquirer

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer -> API Gateway / Ingestion Container: Sends payment authorization requests [HTTPS/TLS 1.3]
- API Gateway / Ingestion Container -> High-Performance Scoring Engine: Routes validated payloads [Internal VPC gRPC using Protocol Buffers]
- API Gateway / Ingestion Container -> Redis: Performs deduplication and idempotency checks [Internal TCP]

## Technology Stack
- AWS API Gateway & Envoy proxy: Provides edge routing, circuit breaking, and low-latency gRPC connection pooling
- Protocol Buffers: Minimizes serialization overhead to meet the 50 ms P99 latency target
- W3C Trace Context & AWS X-Ray: Enables distributed tracing for 7-year auditability
- Redis (Native Envoy Integration): Handles sliding-window idempotency checks and request deduplication
- GitOps & OPA/Rego: Automates configuration management and policy enforcement for a 3-engineer team

## Rationale
This architecture uses Envoy proxy and Protocol Buffers to achieve sub-50ms latency at 3,000 RPS within a strict budget. Edge-level security controls, strict payload validation, and GitOps automation ensure PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance while remaining maintainable for a three-engineer team.

High-Performance Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The High-Performance Scoring Engine screens real-time card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud within strict latency and compliance constraints. It evaluates transactions using hot-reloadable models while maintaining high availability and auditability.

## Key Elements
- High-Performance Scoring Engine (AWS ECS on Fargate container using Clean Architecture / Ports and Adapters)
- Feature Store (Redis with local in-memory LRU cache)
- API Gateway / Ingestion Container (Envoy proxy / AWS API Gateway)
- Async Event Bus (AWS SQS / EventBridge)
- Model & Rule Registry Container
- Audit & Compliance Storage (AWS S3 with Object Lock and Parquet format)

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> High-Performance Scoring Engine: Routes authorization requests [gRPC over internal VPC]
- High-Performance Scoring Engine -> Feature Store: Fetches transaction features [Redis Protocol with strict 15ms timeout budget]
- High-Performance Scoring Engine -> Async Event Bus: Publishes transaction decisions and audit events [AWS SDK / JSON over SQS]
- High-Performance Scoring Engine -> Audit & Compliance Storage: Persists immutable input snapshots and model versions [AWS SDK / HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS on Fargate: Provides scalable, containerized execution with predictable resource bounds and cost control within the 25,000 EUR budget.
- gRPC & Protocol Buffers: Ensures low-latency communication (<50ms P99) and strict schema validation between services.
- Redis & Local LRU Cache: Delivers sub-millisecond feature retrieval while protecting against downstream latency spikes.
- OpenTelemetry: Enables distributed tracing and high-priority metrics for rapid MTTR by a three-person engineering team.
- AWS S3 with Object Lock: Guarantees tamper-evident, 7-year retention for regulatory compliance (R-06).

## Rationale
This architecture uses containerized microservices with strict timeout budgeting, fail-fast startup gates, and fallback mechanisms to meet sub-50ms latency and 99.99% availability constraints. Clean architecture principles and automated contract testing ensure maintainability and zero-downtime deployments for a lean three-person engineering team within a fixed budget.

Feature Store.analysis:
## Overview
The system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real-time and provides case management for human analysts. It processes financial transactions under strict compliance, latency, and budget constraints.

## Key Elements
- High-Performance Scoring Engine (AWS ECS on Fargate)
- Feature Store (AWS ElastiCache for Redis)
- Cold Historical Feature Storage (Amazon S3 / DynamoDB)
- Async Event Bus (AWS EventBridge / SQS)
- API Gateway / Ingestion Container (AWS API Gateway / Envoy proxy)
- Fraud Analyst (Person)

## Relationships
- API Gateway / Ingestion Container -> High-Performance Scoring Engine: Forwards authorization requests [HTTPS / gRPC]
- High-Performance Scoring Engine -> Feature Store (AWS ElastiCache for Redis): Fetches operational features using batch pipelining [Redis Protocol]
- Feature Store -> Async Event Bus: Publishes immutable point-in-time feature snapshots [AWS SDK / JSON over TLS]
- High-Performance Scoring Engine -> Cold Historical Feature Storage: Fallback lookup for historical features [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ElastiCache for Redis: In-memory feature store chosen for sub-millisecond retrieval latency.
- Dual-Tier Storage (Redis + S3/DynamoDB): Balances ultra-low latency operational needs with 7-year audit requirements within budget.
- Protocol Buffers & Schema Registry: Ensures strict payload serialization and prevents schema drift across services.
- AWS ECS on Fargate: Serverless container management minimizing operational overhead for a 3-engineer team.

## Rationale
This architecture achieves sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 requests per second using Redis pipelining and an L1 cache, while remaining within the 25,000 EUR budget through managed AWS services. It guarantees PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability via cryptographic key tokenization, immutable snapshots, and dual-tier storage.

## Overview
The Case Management Web Application provides a secure interface for fraud analysts to review suspicious payment transactions. It utilizes a lightweight Backend-for-Frontend architecture to ensure strict data masking and compliance.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst (Human User)
- Case Management Web Application (AWS ECS on Fargate BFF container)
- Frontend Static Assets (AWS S3 & Amazon CloudFront SPA)
- Downstream Services (Async Event Bus & Tamper-Evident Audit Storage)
- Monitoring & Security (AWS CloudWatch, AWS X-Ray, AWS Inspector/Trivy)

## Relationships
- Fraud Analyst -> Amazon CloudFront: Accesses review interface [HTTPS/TLS]
- Case Management Web Application -> Async Event Bus: Consumes case events and publishes analyst resolutions [AWS SQS/SNS]
- Case Management Web Application -> Audit & Compliance Storage: Writes immutable audit logs of analyst actions [S3 API/HTTPS]
- AWS CloudWatch -> Case Management Web Application: Scrapes RED method operational metrics [CloudWatch Agent]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS on Fargate: Hosts the Backend-for-Frontend API with low operational overhead
- Amazon S3 & CloudFront: Hosts decoupled SPA frontend static assets to reduce container load
- Redis: Manages stateless session storage for horizontal scaling
- OpenAPI: Enforces schema validation and contract testing between BFF and services
- AWS X-Ray & CloudWatch: Provides distributed tracing and RED method metrics monitoring
- Trivy / AWS Inspector: Performs automated vulnerability scanning and SBOM management

## Rationale
This architecture decouples static UI assets from backend API logic, minimizing resource consumption and keeping operational overhead manageable for a three-engineer team. It enforces strict data tokenization and immutable audit logging at the BFF boundary, ensuring full PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability within budget.

Audit & Compliance Storage.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to prevent fraud and manage suspicious reviews. It ensures strict regulatory compliance, low-latency scoring, and robust tamper-evident auditing within a fixed infrastructure budget.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst (User)
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer (External System)
- API Gateway / Ingestion Container (AWS API Gateway / Envoy proxy)
- High-Performance Scoring Engine (AWS ECS on Fargate)
- Feature Store (Redis)
- Async Event Bus (AWS EventBridge / SQS)
- Case Management Web Application (AWS ECS on Fargate)
- Model & Rule Registry Container (Container Service)
- Audit & Compliance Storage (AWS S3 with Object Lock and Parquet format)
- Configuration & Secrets Management (AWS Secrets Manager / Parameter Store)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer -> API Gateway / Ingestion Container: Sends authorization requests [HTTPS/REST]
- API Gateway / Ingestion Container -> High-Performance Scoring Engine: Forwards authorization requests [gRPC]
- High-Performance Scoring Engine <-> Feature Store: Fetches and updates user features [Redis Protocol]
- High-Performance Scoring Engine -> Async Event Bus: Publishes scoring decisions and audit logs [AWS SQS/SNS]
- Async Event Bus -> Audit & Compliance Storage: Streams immutable audit records [AWS SQS/SNS]
- Fraud Analyst -> Case Management Web Application: Reviews suspicious transactions [HTTPS]
- Case Management Web Application -> High-Performance Scoring Engine: Updates case statuses and feedback [HTTPS/REST]

## Technology Stack
- Cloud Infrastructure: AWS (Region: eu-west-1) chosen for managed scalability and compliance features.
- Compute: AWS ECS on Fargate for containerized microservices without server management overhead.
- Storage & Audit: AWS S3 with Object Lock (Compliance Mode) and Parquet format for tamper-evident 7-year retention.
- Query & Analytics: Amazon Athena with Partition Projection and predefined views for cost-controlled serverless querying.
- In-Memory Data Store: Redis for sub-millisecond feature retrieval supporting P99 < 50ms latency.
- Messaging: AWS SQS/SNS with Dead-Letter Queues (DLQ) for asynchronous decoupled event processing.
- Infrastructure as Code: Terraform with prevent-destroy guards to secure compliance configurations.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless and managed AWS services to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team while keeping costs within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget. S3 Object Lock and Athena ensure strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability without sacrificing query performance.

Configuration & Secrets Management.analysis:
## Overview
The Configuration & Secrets Management component securely provides dynamic settings and sensitive credentials to the real-time payment fraud screening platform in AWS eu-west-1. It ensures zero-downtime rule updates, strict auditability, and sub-50ms decision latency within a fixed budget of 25,000 EUR per month.

## Key Elements
* AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store: Stores non-sensitive application configurations and feature flags.
* AWS Secrets Manager: Manages sensitive credentials and API keys with native AWS Lambda rotation.
* High-Performance Scoring Engine (AWS ECS on Fargate): Consumes and caches configurations locally in-memory.
* Git-Ops / Infrastructure-as-Code Pipeline: Acts as the single source of truth and enforces CI/CD schema validation.
* Amazon CloudWatch: Monitors cache age, fallback activation, and schema validation failure metrics.

## Relationships
* High-Performance Scoring Engine polls AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store and AWS Secrets Manager using HTTPS over AWS PrivateLink.
* Git-Ops Pipeline pushes validated configurations to AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store via AWS SDK / API.
* High-Performance Scoring Engine emits operational telemetry to Amazon CloudWatch via AWS SDK.

## Technology Stack
* AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store & AWS Secrets Manager: Chosen for secure separation of concerns and compliance with PCI-DSS Level 1.
* In-Memory Caching with TTL: Implemented in the scoring engine to prevent remote latency bottlenecks and guarantee P99 latency below 50 ms.
* Git-Ops / IaC (GitHub / GitLab CI): Selected to provide version control, automated schema validation, and traceability for a 3-engineer team.
* Amazon CloudWatch Metrics & Alarms: Utilized for automated observability of cache fallbacks and configuration health.

## Rationale
This architecture decouples remote configuration fetches from the hot scoring path via local caching, ensuring high performance and availability. It supports a 3-engineer team and strict PCI-DSS auditability through Git-Ops immutability and automated monitoring.
